The short answer on Wisry vs Holo: both use AI to produce marketing content from your brand inputs, but they start from different premises and solve different problems. Wisry reverse-engineers the ads already winning in your market, then launches campaigns to Meta and Google and optimizes toward ROAS. Holo turns your website URL into ads, social posts, and emails, a broader content engine built for founders who want volume across every channel. [...] |  | Wisry | Holo |
 --- 
| Core approach | Research-first: clones angles already winning in your market | Generation-first: turns your URL into content across all channels |
| Competitor ad research | Yes. Competitor Intel reads Meta and TikTok ad libraries | No; starts from your website, not the market |
| Static ad creative | Yes | Yes |
| Video / UGC ads | Yes, scene-by-scene with brand memory | Yes, UGC-style video with AI presenters |
| Social posts | No | Yes. Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X and more |
| Email / newsletters | No | Yes. Welcome flows, promos, sequences |
| Launches to Meta | Yes | No; you download and publish manually |
| Launches to Google | Yes | No |
| ROAS optimization | Yes. Agents monitor and optimize campaigns | No | [...] ### Can Wisry generate social posts and emails like Holo?

No. Wisry is focused on paid ad creative, statics and video, for Meta and Google campaigns. If you need organic social content or email sequences, Holo covers those channels and Wisry does not.

### Is Wisry a good Holo alternative for ecommerce brands?

Wisry is a strong alternative for ecommerce brands that want their ad creative backed by competitor research, not a blank brief. Wisry’s Competitor Intel reads the ads already winning in your market before generating anything, and the campaign-launch agent ships directly to Meta and Google and optimizes for ROAS, a workflow Holo does not offer.

“Clone winning ads” makes some marketers flinch, so let's separate two things.
Copying is taking a competitor's ad and swapping the logo. It's lazy, it's legally gray, and it won't sound like you anyway.
Cloning is closer to what strong media buyers have always done: identify the angle, hook structure, and offer framing the market has already rewarded, then rebuild the ad from scratch with your product, your proof, and your voice.
The structure is public information. The execution is where the brand lives.
Swipe for the five steps. Where do you draw the line between inspiration and imitation?

Your best customer might be hiding inside your worst-looking ad.
One of the biggest mistakes I see in advertising is judging a creative by how “professional” it looks.
A polished ad can get ignored. A simple, ugly-looking ad can generate sales.
Why? Because performance isn't a design competition.
Sometimes the ad that feels too simple, too direct, or even a little ugly is the one that speaks most clearly to the customer.
That’s why I’d rather test 10 different creative angles than assume I already know what will work.
Don't optimize for what looks good to you. Optimize for what your market responds to.
Which one would you bet on: A or B? 👇
